data.name: List Rows (Read)
data.description:
Retrieves the rows (records) from the first sheet of the Spreadsheet API.
Documentation: testsp - API Documentation / Making Requests
Quick Start:
- Send a GET request to the endpoint below.
- If your API is configured to require authentication include Basic auth (username & password).
Parameters Explained:
- limit (optional): Maximum number of rows to return. Default: 100. Use integer values (e.g., 50).
- offset (optional): Number of rows to skip (for pagination). Default: 0.
- sheet (optional): If your spreadsheet has multiple worksheets, some APIs allow selecting sheet by name; the example spreadsheet's primary endpoint operates on the first sheet by default.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 401 Unauthorized: No Authorization header or invalid credentials. Use Basic auth with correct username/password.
- 400 Bad Request: limit or offset not valid integers.
- 500 Internal Server Error: Try again later or contact sheet2api support.
Edge Cases:
- Empty sheets return an empty array [].
- Cells with empty values may be omitted or present with empty strings depending on the sheet contents.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- No public rate limits are documented on this page. Check your sheet2api account dashboard or contact support for quota details.
data.evaluateGuide:

Use for: read spreadsheet rows, paginate records, select a worksheet

data.name: List / Read Rows (Sheet)
data.description:
Returns all rows from a worksheet (sheet) in the spreadsheet as JSON. Supports filtering by column (use the column header as a query parameter), wildcard searches, negative matches, and relational operators for numeric comparisons.
Documentation: https://sheet2api.com/docs/requests/FgI6zV8qT121/characters/
Quick Start:
- Method: GET
- URL: {{baseUrl}}/v1/{{workbookId}}/{{sheetName}}/
- No body required. If your API requires authentication, include HTTP Basic Authorization as described in the docs.
Parameters Explained:
- workbookId (required, path) - The unique ID for your Spreadsheet API (example: FgI6zV8qT121). Replace with your API's workbook id.
- sheetName (required, path) - The worksheet name (sheet title). If it contains spaces, URL-encode it (e.g., "Looney Tunes" → "Looney%20Tunes").
- Column filters (optional, query string) - Use the spreadsheet column header name as the query parameter. Example: ?Name=Bugs%20Bunny filters rows where the Name column equals "Bugs Bunny".
  - Wildcard search: include an asterisk * anywhere in the value. Example: ?Name=Bugs*Bunny.
  - Negative search: prefix value with ! to exclude. Example: ?Name=!Bugs%20Bunny.
  - Relational (numeric) operators: prefix the value with <, >, <=, or >=. Example: ?age<20.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 401 Unauthorized: Your API is secured and you did not send Basic auth credentials (username:password base64 encoded). Provide credentials or disable auth for this API.
- 404 Not Found: workbookId or sheetName is incorrect — check your API URL and ensure the sheet exists and is spelled/URL-encoded correctly.
- 429 Too Many Requests: You exceeded your plan quota — see your account dashboard or upgrade your plan.
Edge Cases:
- Column names with special characters or spaces must be URL-encoded when used in a path or query string.
- Searching numeric columns with relational operators requires the column values to be numeric in the sheet.
- Large sheets might be cached; recent edits may take a short time to propagate depending on caching settings.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Quota depends on your plan (see https://sheet2api.com/pricing/). Exceeding quota returns 429. Default caching and quota policies apply per account.
data.evaluateGuide:
Returns worksheet rows as JSON from a Sheet2API spreadsheet, with filtering, wildcard matching, comparisons, pagination, and sorting through query parameters.
Use for: filter sheet rows, search records, paginate results, sort worksheet data
Not supported: writing rows, deleting records, editing formulas

data.name: Read Dataset Rows (SODA 2.1 resource endpoint)
data.description:
Retrieves rows from a Socrata dataset (SODA Consumer API / Resource endpoint).
Documentation: https://dev.socrata.com/docs/endpoints
Quick Start:
- Use a dataset identifier (eight-character identifier, e.g. 4tka-6guv).
- For simple reads you do not need user authentication for public datasets; include an application token in X-App-Token for higher rate limits.
- Use SoQL parameters (e.g. $select, $where, $limit, $offset, $order, $q) as query parameters.
Parameters Explained:
- datasetId (path, required): The dataset identifier (example: 4tka-6guv).
- $select (query, optional): Comma-separated list of columns to return. Default: all columns.
- $where (query, optional): SoQL WHERE clause for filtering rows.
- $limit (query, optional): Number of rows to return. Default: 1000; max depends on endpoint/version.
- $offset (query, optional): Result offset for paging. Default: 0.
- $order (query, optional): SoQL ordering expression (e.g. :id or column DESC).
- $q (query, optional): Full-text search over dataset fields.
- X-App-Token (header, optional): Application token for higher throttling; not required for public reads.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 400 Bad Request: Malformed SoQL parameter; check URL-encoding and SoQL syntax.
- 401 Unauthorized: Trying to read a private dataset without auth.
- 403 Forbidden: CORS/JSONP dropped authentication — use server-side calls for authenticated reads.
- 404 Not Found: Invalid datasetId or dataset removed.
Edge Cases:
- Ordering is not guaranteed unless you specify $order (use a stable key like :id).
- Large limits may be capped by server; use $offset paging.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Unauthenticated requests use shared rate limits; supplying X-App-Token attributes requests to your app and increases quota.
data.evaluateGuide:
Queries a Socrata dataset resource and returns matching rows using SoQL query parameters. Use it to retrieve, filter, select, sort, or paginate public Colorado data.
Use for: query dataset rows, filter public data, select fields, paginate results
Not supported: inserting records, updating datasets, managing dataset definitions

data.name: List Rows (Read)
data.description:
Retrieve rows from a worksheet (the default is the first sheet).
Documentation: https://sheet2api.com/documentation/
Quick Start:
- Use the generated Spreadsheet API URL (example: https://sheet2api.com/v1/FgI6zV8qT121/characters/)
- If your API is protected enable Authorization (Basic) as configured in your account
- Optional query params can filter, paginate or sort results
Parameters Explained:
- apiId (required): Your spreadsheet API identifier (part of the generated URL). Example: FgI6zV8qT121
- apiSlug (required): The API/endpoint slug (usually the API name). Example: characters
- sheetName (optional path): Worksheet name (URL-encoded) to operate on a specific sheet. If omitted, the API will use the first sheet.
- apiKey (optional): API key when the sheet is protected via API key (some accounts may use API keys instead of Basic auth)
- limit (optional): Maximum number of rows returned. Default: service default (commonly 100)
- offset / page (optional): Pagination controls. Use offset or page depending on your usage.
- field filters (optional): Any column name can be used as a query param to filter rows, e.g. ?Name=Bugs%20Bunny
- q / search (optional): Free-text search parameter (implementation varies)
- sortBy, sortOrder (optional): Sorting fields (e.g., sortBy=Name&sortOrder=asc)
- fields (optional): Comma-separated list of columns to return
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 401 Unauthorized: API is protected and Authorization header is missing or invalid — set Basic credentials via the collection variables or include api_key if configured.
- 429 Too Many Requests: You exceeded plan quota — upgrade or wait for quota reset.
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid query parameter (check parameter names and encoding).
Edge Cases:
- If multiple worksheets exist you may either call the base URL (first sheet) or include the sheetName path segment (URL encoded).
- Filtering by column uses exact match unless using advanced query features supported by your account.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Rate limits depend on your plan (see account/pricing). Exceeding quota returns 429.
data.evaluateGuide:
Retrieves worksheet rows as JSON from a generated Sheet2API endpoint, with optional filtering, pagination, and sorting.
Use for: read sheet rows, filter records, paginate data, sort results
Not supported: writing rows, deleting records, modifying worksheet structure

data.name: List Rows (Read)
data.description:
Returns the rows from the default (first) sheet of the Spreadsheet API as JSON.
Documentation: https://sheet2api.com/docs/FgI6zV8qT121/characters/
Quick Start:
- HTTP Method: GET
- URL: {{baseUrl}}/v1/FgI6zV8qT121/characters/
- No request body required. Use query string filters to restrict results.
Parameters Explained:
- Name (optional): Example column-based filter. Replace Name with any column title from your sheet to filter by that column. Supports wildcard * (e.g. Name=Bugs*Bunny) and negation ! (e.g. Name=!Bugs Bunny). For numeric columns you may use relational operators by prefixing value with <, >, <=, >= (e.g. age>20).
- OtherColumn (optional): Any other sheet column can be used as a query parameter in the same way as Name.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 401 Unauthorized: Your spreadsheet API is configured to require authentication but Authorization header is missing or invalid. Use Basic auth (username:password base64 encoded) or supply {{username}} & {{password}} in your client.
- 400 Bad Request: Malformed query parameter. Ensure column names are spelled exactly as in the header row and values are URL-encoded.
- 500 Internal Server Error: Transient server or upstream Sheets error — retry after a short delay.
Edge Cases:
- Column names with spaces or special characters must be URL-encoded in query string (e.g. Favourite Thing -> Favourite%20Thing).
- When multiple rows match the filters, all matching rows are returned.
- If the sheet is empty the response will be an empty array.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Rate limits are not listed on this page. If you see 429 responses, implement exponential backoff. (Check account dashboard for plan-specific limits.)
data.evaluateGuide:
Returns rows from the default worksheet of a Sheet2API spreadsheet as JSON. Query parameters can restrict and organize the returned records.
Use for: read worksheet rows, filter by columns, paginate records, sort results
Not supported: creating rows, updating values, changing formulas

Quick Start:

Parameters Explained:
- nativeTableName (path): The native Ramp table slug (e.g., users).
- includeAllReferencedRows (query): If true, include the full set of referenced rows in each cell rather than a truncated subset.
- pageSize and start: Pagination controls.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 404 Not Found: Native table not found.

data.name: Get dataset rows (SODA resource read endpoint)
data.description:
Legacy SODA2-style resource endpoint for querying datasets using URL query parameters (SoQL via query string). Supports .json, .csv, .geojson (format selected by extension). This endpoint is widely used and remains available for many datasets.
Documentation: https://dev.socrata.com/foundry/soda.demo.socrata.com/4tka-6guv
Quick Start:
- Use {{baseUrl}}/resource/{{datasetId}}.json for JSON output.
- Provide query parameters such as $select, $where, $limit, $offset, $order, $group, and $q.
- For large/complex queries prefer SODA3 /api/v3/views/{id}/query.json (POST).
Parameters Explained:
- $select (query): Comma-separated list of columns to return.
- $where (query): SoQL WHERE clause (no leading WHERE).
- $limit (query): Maximum number of rows to return. Default varies.
- $offset (query): Row offset for pagination.
- $order (query): SoQL ORDER BY clause.
- $q (query): Full-text search across dataset.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid parameter syntax; validate SoQL and URL-encoded values.
- 413 Request Entity Too Large: Asking too many rows without limits.
- 401 Unauthorized / 403 Forbidden: Resource requires authentication or proper permissions.
Edge Cases:
- Query string length limits in GET requests — use POST SODA3 for long queries.
- Some domains return different field names or computed fields; check metadata.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Call quota limits may be applied per domain or per application token.
data.evaluateGuide:
Queries a Socrata dataset resource and returns rows in the selected format, including CSV, using SoQL query parameters.
Use for: export dataset rows, filter open data, select fields, paginate results
Not supported: inserting records, updating datasets, changing dataset schemas

data.name: SODA Read API - Query Rows (CSV / XML) Export
data.description:
SODA resource endpoint supporting alternate output formats via file extension: .csv, .xml. Useful for quick exports using the SODA style query parameters.
Documentation: https://data.transportation.gov/d/dkgi-gbeh
Quick Start:
- To request CSV: GET {{baseUrl}}/resource/{{datasetId}}.csv?$select=year,commodity&$limit=100
Parameters Explained:
- Same query parameters as the JSON SODA endpoint: $select, $where, $limit, $offset, $order.
- format is controlled by the URL extension (.csv or .xml).
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 400 Bad Request: malformed query syntax.
- 415 Unsupported Media Type: requesting unsupported combination of parameters and format.
Edge Cases:
- CSV content is returned as text/csv; non-ASCII characters may be escaped depending on server settings.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Exporting large CSV via the SODA CSV endpoint may be throttled; use rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD for full dataset exports when available.
data.evaluateGuide:
Queries a Socrata resource and exports matching rows as CSV or XML using URL-based SoQL parameters.
Use for: export rows as CSV, export rows as XML, filter survey data, select fields
Not supported: JSON-specific output, inserting records, updating datasets
